elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience"
"upon 30 days' prior written notice to Vendor"
"Vendor shall provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "Vendor may not terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term."
notice is "30 days'", shorter than the 60–90 day fallback window (more favourable to Customer)

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: no early-termination fee is imposed anywhere in the clause

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Vendor may not terminate ... for convenience during a committed term" — no end-of-term Vendor right granted

reasons: The inserted Section 9.4 supplies all four preferred atomic elements: a Customer-only convenience right, 30 days' prior written notice, a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a committed term.
The fallback is not satisfied (notice is 30 rather than 60–90 days and no end-of-term Vendor right), but preferred and fallback are separate bargains and the locked target level is preferred.

Minimal: a single concise insertion filling a genuine gap (Section 8.1 gives a three-year term with no convenience exit); Sections 9.1–9.3 and 9.5 are untouched and no boilerplate or new exceptions were added.
Preserves intent: uses defined terms Fees, Order Form, Vendor; numbering 9.4 fits the existing sequence between 9.3 and 9.5; no contradiction or dangling mechanic introduced.
